Subject: Bluecrest renewal — sequencing & one-off term tweak

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the productive call today. Quick summary and ask so we have a clean thread for legal:

- Bluecrest intent: renew Redwood services, expand embedding capacity by +2.5M units, and move to an 18-month term rather than 12.
- Impact area: Exhibit B (usage tiers), Order Form (capacity lines), and one limited MSA clause tweak (Section 6.2 SLAs — add narrower credit carve).

Attached: initial MSA redline (Bluecrest_MSA_v3_redline.pdf) and a draft order form worksheet (OrderForm_Bluecrest_2029.xlsx).

As next steps, can you confirm: 1) procurement contact who will own contract redlines (CC'd or reply), and 2) whether the 18-month term is a firm ask vs preference? If firm, we will model pricing for the extended term and propose a pro-rated uplift for the extra 6 months.

I want to align on sequencing: our recommendation is sign MSA amendment and order form together, but if procurement needs separate tracks we can accommodate a two-step path (OrderForm sign then MSA technical exhibit follow).

Open to a quick 30m tomorrow if that helps.

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Subject: internal: Bluecrest MSA redline & term economics (draft strategy)

Jasmine / Marcus / Tessa — quick internal note before I craft a formal response to Bluecrest procurement.

Summary of ask: 18-month term + +2.5M embedding units. Exhibit B update and a narrower SLA credit request.

Legal posture and recommended concessions:
- Keep MSA changes minimal. We can accept targeted edits to Section 6.2 that define "service interruption" but avoid opening general availability or force majeure windows. Markus (legal) should take the redline and convert to clean amendment language.
- Pricing: if Bluecrest requires 18 months, propose a blended effective per-unit price that is ~8% below the 12-month sticker (to reflect committed volume). Cap the blended discount to the uplift and require any additional burst consumption be charged at standard overage rates.
- Ramp: require a 3-month ramp schedule in Exhibit B (monthly minimums at 30%/60%/100% of forecast) to avoid immediate capacity pressure. If they can't accept a ramp, price should include a short-term surge fee for the first 90 days.
- Sequencing: prefer single DocuSign envelope (MSA amendment + Order Form). That reduces administrative churn for both sides.

Requested from Ops: Marcus, can you confirm availability on Dedicated pools for the proposed ramp profile? Need a quick capacity check before we commit.

I'll draft an answer to procurement that outlines the above and attaches a cleaned MSA amendment redline for Markus to sign off.

-Neha
Sr. Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Hi Olivia / procurement team —

Appreciate the quick turn. Attached is an updated package:
- Bluecrest_MSA_v3_redline.pdf (cleaned by Markus; highlights retained on Section 6.2 language)
- OrderForm_Bluecrest_2029.xlsx (updated with 18-month term rows and blended pricing proposal)
- ExhibitB-usage-tiers.xlsx (we incorporated your forecast into the ramp table)

Key points from our side:
1) Term & pricing: We can do 18 months with a blended unit price (see OrderForm tab 'Pricing'). The blended discount is capped as discussed — details in cell range D42:D48.
2) Ramp: We included a 3-month ramp (30% / 60% / 100%) in Exhibit B. If you need immediate 100% on day one, we will need to add a temporary surge fee for months 1–3 (worksheet has both options).
3) SLA language: Markus tightened the definition of "service interruption" and added an explicit exclusion for scheduled maintenance with notice. Legal retained a narrow credit formula rather than open-ended metrics.
4) DocuSign: we can originate a single envelope covering the MSA amendment + Order Form and send to procurement@bluecrest.com once you confirm the signers. Who will be the final signer on your side?

Proposed timeline:
- Confirm signers & final ramp choice by Mon 8/19
- DocuSign envelope sent Tue 8/20
- Execution target: 8/22–8/23

If you'd like a short call to walk procurement through the workbook, Marcus and I are free tomorrow afternoon.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
